Where you will go

Three countries, one seamless trip

Kenya is our home ground and where most trips begin. Tanzania and Uganda combine with it easily — we handle the border crossings, internal flights and permits for you.

Kenya

The Maasai Mara, elephants under Kilimanjaro at Amboseli, the flamingo lakes of the Rift Valley and the white sand of Diani Beach.

  • Arrive: Nairobi — Jomo Kenyatta Intl (NBO)
  • Entry: eTA online before you fly
  • Best months: Jul–Oct (migration), Jan–Feb (clear skies)

Tanzania

The endless Serengeti, the wildlife-packed Ngorongoro Crater, elephant country in Tarangire and the spice island of Zanzibar.

  • Arrive: Kilimanjaro Intl (JRO) or Zanzibar (ZNZ)
  • Entry: eVisa online before you fly
  • Best months: Jun–Oct (dry season), Jan–Feb (calving)

Uganda

Mountain gorillas in Bwindi’s misty forest, chimpanzees in Kibale and the Nile thundering through Murchison Falls.

  • Arrive: Entebbe Intl (EBB)
  • Entry: eVisa online — no visa on arrival
  • Best months: Jun–Sep and Dec–Feb (drier trails)

Before you fly

Travel info for international visitors

Most of our guests fly in from the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Ireland. Wherever you are coming from, the routine is the same: apply online before you fly, and only ever on the official government site.

Kenya — eTA

Kenya replaced the paper visa with an Electronic Travel Authorisation. Apply online at least a few days before departure and carry the approval when you fly into Nairobi (NBO).

Official portal: etakenya.go.ke

Tanzania — eVisa

Apply for an eVisa before travel for Kilimanjaro (JRO), Dar es Salaam or Zanzibar. US citizens usually need the multiple-entry visa. Allow at least two weeks for processing.

Official portal: visa.immigration.go.tz

Uganda — eVisa

Uganda no longer issues visas on arrival at Entebbe (EBB) — apply online in advance. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required for entry.

Official portal: visas.immigration.go.ug

Money & payments

  • All our prices are in US dollars, per person sharing.
  • Pay your deposit by card or international bank transfer.
  • US dollars are widely accepted on the ground; cards work in lodges and towns.
  • A 30% deposit confirms your trip; the balance is due 45 days before departure.

Health & packing

  • Yellow fever certificate: required for Uganda, and for Tanzania if arriving from a risk country.
  • Talk to your doctor about malaria prophylaxis — all three countries are malaria areas.
  • Neutral-coloured clothing, a warm layer for early game drives, soft-sided luggage.
  • Passport valid 6+ months with at least one blank page.

Getting here

  • Nairobi (NBO) — direct flights from New York, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Doha, Dubai and more.
  • Kilimanjaro (JRO) — via Amsterdam, Doha, Istanbul or Nairobi.
  • Entebbe (EBB) — via Brussels, Amsterdam, Doha, Dubai or Nairobi.
  • We meet you at arrivals, whatever time your flight lands.

Good to know

Questions travellers ask us

When is the best time to come?

For the Great Migration in the Maasai Mara and Serengeti, July to October is peak season. January and February are warm, dry and excellent for wildlife with fewer visitors. The long rains (April–May) bring lush scenery and the lowest prices, and game viewing is still very good.

Are your safaris private or group?

Both. Every tour can run as a private trip for just your party — your own vehicle and driver-guide throughout — or on scheduled small-group departures with a maximum of seven guests per vehicle, so everyone gets a window seat.

What is included in the tour prices?

Accommodation as listed, park and conservation fees, game drives in a 4×4 with a professional driver-guide, airport transfers, and meals as shown in each itinerary. International flights, visas/eTAs, travel insurance and personal items are not included.

How do I book, and when do I pay?

Send an enquiry from this page. We reply by email with availability and a confirmed itemised quote. A 30% deposit by card or bank transfer confirms your booking; the balance is due 45 days before departure. Nothing is charged from this website.

Can you combine countries in one trip?

Yes — Kenya + Tanzania is our most popular combination (Mara and Serengeti are the same ecosystem), and Uganda adds beautifully for gorillas. We arrange the internal flights, border logistics and the separate Tanzania visa alongside the Kenya eTA and Uganda eVisa.

Is East Africa safe for visitors?

The safari regions welcome well over a million visitors a year. You are met at the airport, driven by our own guides, and stay in established lodges and camps. We brief you fully before you travel and are on call around the clock while you are with us.
